question: Hello doctor,I am a 29-year-old female. I was just diagnosed with chronic urticaria. doctor_response: Hello,  Welcome to ChatDoctor. RAST is a highly accurate test. If the test is positive for a specific allergen, it shows that you are sensitized to that particular allergen. This means that you may mount an allergic response when you are exposed to that allergen. However, it does not mean that you will necessarily have an allergic reaction to that substance and, nor does it mean that any reactions will be severe. If the test is negative, it means that one does not have the ability to mount an allergic reaction to that allergen and any symptoms one may be experiencing are probably not due to an allergic reaction to that substance. However, the results of the RAST need to be interpreted in conjunction with your clinical history. e.g the presence of allergy to some or few allergens which may possibly be present either in the environment or food does not necessarily mean that they are responsible for the symptoms because if they are not even present in the environment or food of an individual, then they are irrelevant. In your case, an elimination diet has not helped thus proving the fact that RAST test results should be carefully interpreted along with clinical history and does not necessarily mean that you will necessarily have an allergic reaction to the substance that you tested. Angioedema is frequently associated with urticaria. Pathogenesis is the same for both urticaria as well as angioedema. The presence of angioedema does not always mean that it is a part of anaphylaxis. Angioedema can be a part of anaphylaxis in those individuals who have a severe allergic reaction to an allergen with high levels of antibodies circulating in the blood. Since you have only class 1 and 2 level antibodies therefore it is unlike that these antigens or allergens would cause anaphylaxis.
response: 1. The RAST test is very specific and usually accurate. However, the sensitivity of the test depends upon the level of antibody in your blood. So when they say that the level of allergen is less than certain amount, it doesn't mean that you will not be reactive to it. You may be mildly or moderately reactive to it. 2. Angiodema is not a common complication of food allergy and anaphylaxis. It is more likely to occur due to insect stings or some medications like beta-blockers etc.

question: Hello doctor,When I was 11 years old, I was knocked off my bike and cracked my front tooth in half horizontally, shortly after the dentist fixed it. Any trauma to the tooth generally has long-term consequences like tooth discoloration, etc. As you said that your tooth was fractured, it might have led to a slight injury to the pulp or even if not so, the fracture line would have been close to the pulp. He would prescribe a vitality test of the tooth and also would get an x-ray for the tooth. By that way, he would come to know if the tooth is dead or still vital and accordingly will propose treatment. If the tooth is vital, he will put some medication over the pulp to let it heal and then fill with the pulp friendly restoration. However, if the tooth is dead, I would suggest you to go for the root canal treatment (after evaluating the condition of the tooth and soft tissue). Meanwhile, keep your oral hygiene good, brush twice daily and floss regularly. Use mouth rinses to clean the mouth after meals.

Fibrotic scars can be very bad if they form too much collagen, however this doesn't happen in most cases.2) Your doctor was correct to say that this was likely due to an old infection. question: Hello doctor,How accurate are skin prick tests for predicting positive reactions? My family is interested in a pet and I have had negative skin prick and blood work tests for dander. doctor_response: Hi. Skin prick allergy testing is one of the most accurate ways of diagnosing the allergen, one is sensitive to. It is definitely more accurate than blood immunoCAP testing (blood allergy testing). Skin prick testing checks your sensitivity to the protein in question. Even if sensitive, it need not mean you are allergic. Whereby, a positive result need not always mean you will get allergy with the protein. It means that your immune system is sensitised to that allergen and that an allergy can occur in subsequent exposures to the allergen. A negative in skin prick testing will mean that you are not sensitive to that protein and that you will not end with an allergy upon its exposure. This is true. But it is specific for the particular type of allergen. What all animal danders were included in your profile and what was the response to each? Is there a photograph or record of the wheal or flare that developed after each prick? Was the test read by a clinical allergist or immunologist and were you provided a report as to that you are not allergic to any animal dander? Were you diagnosed with pollen allergy or sensitivity? Have you observed any symptoms of allergy while in gardens or bushy areas? Or in any particular season? Does any one else in your family have allergies?

It should be done by an expert dermatologist or immunologist as they know how to interpret them. You may need to repeat once or twice to get correct result. But generally they are very reliable in prediction of allergies. Hope this answers your question.

question: Hello doctor,How can I figure out my conception date? My last menstrual period was three months back. I had my dating ultrasound and it put the GA at 9 weeks and 3 days. Other than that it is easy to remember last date of menses and easy for calculation, so we are calculating pregnancy from last day of menses. In technical terms there are two age of pregnancy one is gestational age and other is embryonic age. Embryonic age is actual age from conception and gestational age is from last day of menstruation. Now what is importance of this date? It means if delivery pain starts near this date then let it happen. response: 1) The most accurate way to calculate the conception date is by counting from the first day of your last normal menses (LNM). This would mean that if you have a regular 28-day cycle, then the conception date could be calculated as 14 days before the expected ovulation day. However, this calculation is not always reliable as not all women have regular cycles with the same length every month. For those who do not have a regular cycle or whose cycles vary in length, the safest way to calculate the conception date is by using the calendar method. 2) The safest days for conception are the 10 to 17 days prior to expected ovulation day.

response: Non-Fasting Blood Test for HIV. The primary blood test for HIV is called \"ELISA\". This test can be done either as a fasting or non-fasting test. The ELISA test is performed by taking a small sample of your blood and then running it through a machine that detects antibodies against HIV. These antibodies are produced by your body in response to the virus. Once these antibodies are detected in your blood, they remain there even if you take medications to treat HIV. Therefore, this test can be used to determine whether you have been infected with HIV. It also gives an indication of how long ago you were exposed to HIV. An additional test called Western Blot is usually performed at the same time as ELISA. It is more sensitive than ELISA and will give a much more accurate result. However, most doctors use the ELISA test

question: Hello doctor,Is HIV RNA, QL TMA accurate after 20 to 21 days of exposure? And also this came with my results. RNA is not detected. No laboratory evidence of HIV infection. There is no current laboratory evidence of HIV infection. Repeat testing on a second specimen is not generally indicated but may be appropriate if there are known risk factors for recent HIV exposure. Other times this test can be useful as a second test after an indeterminate fourth generation HIV screening test or when a positive HIV screening test is followed by a negative confirmatory test (usually a western blot). In the second scenario, if RNA PCR turns up as negative then it suggests that an earlier positive screening test was most likely a false positive.

question: Hi doctor, My husband was diagnosed with APL before six years. He underwent treatment by following the pethema protocol for APL. After consolidation phase, BMA revealed there is still 7% of PML Rara using fish rara test while negative on cytogenetics. doctor_response: Hello, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. Sorry to hear about your husband\\s diagnosis. He is having acute promyelocytic leukemia cancer and it is considered among favorable outcome leukemia. After starting chemotherapy complete remission includes less than 5% blast in bone marrow aspirate, ANC more then 1500, platelets more than 1 lakh, extramedullary hematopoiesis absent and molecular testing negativity. After consolidation chemotherapy, if cytogenetic study remains positive then prognosis cannot be considered good as compared to a negative cytogenetic leukemic patient after chemotherapy and it can be considered here as a minimal residual disease. Treatment was given in the right way along with proper chemotherapy and retinoic acid as well. But you have to discuss your case with your treating oncologist and he will guide you further about what is the future treatment protocol. I hope this helps.
response: 100% recovery from Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) does not occur in majority of patients.  The current standard of care is to maintain the patient on low dose ATRA and chemotherapy(all-trans retinoic acid [ATRA] + anthracyclines/cytosine analogues) until complete remission (CR) is achieved.  CR is defined as absence of blast cells in peripheral blood and bone marrow.  Persistent minimal residual disease (MRD) may be present even after achieving CR. MRD levels can only be detected by molecular methods such as PCR or FISH.  It has been suggested that if MRD levels are less than 1%, then it is likely that the disease is in full remission.  In your husbands case, since the MRD levels are above 1%, further treatment is required.

question: Hello doctor,Can one be color blind if one has 20/20 vision?
doctor_response: Hello, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. Well, for your knowledge color blindness and color deficiency are two different things. You gain color vision due to cone cells in your retina. True color blinds see only black and white. They have no cones or have only blue cones. This is rare and they do not have 20/20 vision they nearly have 20/200. Most others are color deficient people; however, it is erroneously used as a color blind. They have either two types of cones including the blue and all three types of cones. They see the world colored but they have issues with color discrimination. They can have 20/20 vision. For more information consult an eye care ophthalmologist online
response: 1. No, not at all, but it is possible to have normal vision and still be color blind. Color blindness is an inherited condition that affects the way certain colors appear to people with this condition. It is caused by problems in the cells of the retina that respond to light.  The cells are called cones. People who are color blind usually cannot distinguish shades of red, green or blue. Someone with this condition may also have difficulty seeing yellow, brown, and gray. Color blindness can be passed down from parents to their children.

question: Hello doctor,I had two sexual encounters with women whom I do not know their HIV status. Both were vaginal and a condom was worn. In the fourth and fifth weeks, I had a fourth-generation antibody-antigen test performed and it came back negative. Should I be retested again?
doctor_response: Hello,  Welcome to ChatDoctor. It is a good idea to get repeat testing, here is why. The antibody testing at the fourth and fifth weeks can give you some idea of the HIV (human immuno deficiency virus) status, but the one at 12 weeks after the exposure will confirm the negative status completely. The reason being the window period. The window period is a duration where a person can have HIV but still test HIV negative. The fourth generation is antigen-antibody based testing and the best we have so far for screening. When suspected acute HIV infection or high risk exposure, PCR (polymerase chain reaction) is the best in the fourth and fifth weeks post-exposure. Of note, the window period for a fourth-generation antigen-antibody test is short as compared to other HIV tests available (about four weeks). Usually by this time, 95% of infection will be detected in the blood. In general, there is a three month window period for HIV after a given exposure, and therefore for the fouth generation testing to confirm that a person is more than 99.9% infectious. Hence the 12 weeks retesting is recommended. I hope this helps.
response: 1) You have been exposed to risk of acquiring HIV infection but your tests are negative, so don't worry about this.2) It is possible that you have acquired immunity against HIV, or you may not have contracted the virus at all.3) Repeat testing after 3 months will confirm your negative result.4) Repeat testing every 6 months for the next 2 years will give you more assurance of your lack of infection.5) You can get tested annually thereafter.

doctor_response: HiThanks for your querywoman may never need treatment for a bicornuate uterus. If it is required, the surgery is known as a Strassman metroplasty.This surgery may be recommended if a woman has repeated miscarriages and bicornuate uterus is thought to be the cause.Performing this procedure, as a solution to infertility, is controversial, as the majority of research carried out suggests that having a bicornuate uterus will not affect a woman's chances of falling pregnant.Some evidence suggests that problems, such as miscarriage and early birth, are more likely in women with the condition, though it does not rule out a successful pregnancy and natural delivery.Women with a bicornuate uterus who do become pregnant should have additional monitoring and checkups throughout their pregnancy, to minimize risk and identify any problems early on.It's not necessary that all those with this condition will get problems with fertility or pregnancy but the chances are more especially if it's septate uterus where there's full septum diving uterus into two.Sometimes it can't be established on imaging and laparoscopic view may be necessary. response: Yes, if your HSG shows a bicornuate uterus then it means that your uterus is not shaped normally. The normal shape for a female is like a tulip with two flaps at the top which are called cornua. You may have one or two cornua missing as well as a thin wall between the two halves of your uterus. This makes conception difficult because the sperm cannot swim up the fallopian tubes to reach the egg. It also means that if you do become pregnant, the baby will not develop properly in the first months of its life. The best way to correct this problem is to have surgery to remove the wall between the two sides of your uterus and reconnect the two sides. This is called a hysterosalpingogram (HSG). You should discuss this operation with your gynecologist.

question: Hello doctor,Will fertilization occur immediately after an egg is released? And will the ovulation test show positive regardless of fertilization has occurred immediately? I had sex three days ago but the ovulation test still showed positive today. Please suggest.

So you should have sex after two or three days of positive ovulation test. It is the most likely time of ovulation. But it is not confirmatory. Ovulation does not always happens after LH surge. Ovulation test does not have a relation with fertilization. Fertilization may or may not occurs even after ovulation.
response: Hi, Thanks for posting your query. Yes, fertilization occurs immediately after ovulation. The ovulation test detects the LH surge which indicates that ovulation has occurred and hence it would be positive even if there is no fertilization. This is because the ovulation test detects the rise in the LH hormone level which happens immediately after the release of the egg from the ovary. So, the test becomes positive within 1-2 days of ovulation. Hope this helps.

doctor_response: Hello, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. I understand your concerns, vertical heterophoria is a disorder of the mechanisms which maintain the balance of the eye muscles, keeping them on target. Although rare, these can lead to significant distress and dizziness as well. The best test to see if you have heterophoria in any direction is the cover or cover-uncover and alternate cover tests. These should be done with glasses first and then without them. You need the help of another person while doing this at home or can be quickly done at the doctor\\s clinic. 1. Cover test or uncover test - close one of your eyes with your hand while trying to look at an image around six meters away first and then held at 50 cm apart, with both your eyes, then take away the covering hand. If you see the eye that was covered moving, then you have a phoria in the direction opposite the direction in which the eye moved. 2. Alternate cover test - is the same as the cover or uncover tests, only that the covering hand is rapidly moved from eye to eye. This gives a more accurate picture of the type or magnitude of the heterophoria. These are two of the best, safest and economical tests that you can use to diagnose heterophoria. In case you need more information about heterophoria or tests or management options, please send me a scanned copy of your doctors reports and test results. I will do my best to help you with this. doctor_response: Hello. Yes, there have been cases where ANA once positive becomes negative towards the later part. So to conclude, if her ENA is negative and antiphospholipid is negative we should not focus too much on just ANA. question: Hi doctor,According to my LMP now I am 9 weeks pregnant. I went for USG TV 20 days back and it showed that I was 7 weeks and 2 days and now it would be 8 weeks. doctor_response: Hi. At 6 weeks and beyond we expect a fetal pole or yolk sac to be visualized on USG. By 7 weeks, we must see the cardiac activity. If there is no embryo and no heart beat even beyond 7 weeks, we call it a blighted ovum (BO) with only a sac and no contents inside. It can happen due to a chromosomally abnormal gestation and hence does not survive. It regresses on its own. To date your pregnancy, we calculate period of gestation by LMP (last menstrual period) and then confirm it with an earliest scan within 3 months of pregnancy. In case there is no difference between the two dates or a difference is less than a week, we consider the LMP to calculate the expected date of delivery and period of gestation. Do not worry, you can conceive again. But no hope with this pregnancy. Start Folic Acid 5 mg daily for 3 months before next conception. This will help in a healthy embryo, reduce chance of miscarriage and prevent neural defects in the fetus.

The direct Coombs test detects antibody coated on red blood cells. In cold agglutinin disease, the IgM antibody coat the red blood cells. response: Hi there, thanks for your question. A coombs test is done to see if antibodies have been produced against red blood cells. These antibodies are called \"coombs\" antibodies. They can present in different diseases like cold agglutinin disease, autoimmune hemolytic anemia etc. The test has two parts -direct and indirect. In direct test, RBCs are incubated with serum from the patient, and then tested for agglutination (clumping) of RBCs. Indirect test involves mixing of RBCs with normal serum, and then adding the patients serum. This test is more sensitive than direct test, but less specific. So if you have a positive result, it means that you should consult a hematologist as soon as possible for further work up. Hope this helps.

question: Hello doctor,My father is 56 years old and is suffering from a low ejection fraction rate of 25%. Is there any way of recovery?

If the cause is non-ischemic with blockages like DCMP (dilated cardiomyopathy), then there is a chance for improvement with medication. So basically, there may be some improvement with medicines, but whether marked improvement would occur or not will depend on the viability of heart muscle, which can be known on further testing with PET scan. question: Hello doctor,For the past three weeks, I have had my normal right eye floaters seem strange. I noticed peripheral flashes when blinking and walking and quick black narrow lines. doctor_response: Hi. The hollow of the eye is filled with vitreous jelly. With aging, the jelly starts to liquify and separates from its attachments to the retina. This results in a little tug on the retina, resulting in flashes. This phenomenon is known as posterior vitreous detachment or PVD in short. The large floater appears when the PVD is complete, that is, it detaches from its final strong attachment on the optic nerve head in the retina. What you are experiencing is normal aging of the vitreous jelly. Now in this process, sometimes breaks may form in the retina leading to floaters. Floaters may be due to the cells from the back of the retina gaining access to the vitreous cavity through the breaks in the retina. Sometimes floaters may result when the break involves a retinal blood vessel. It is extremely important to get a dilated fundus examination done on an urgent basis to rule out any of the breaks. If found, they can be lasered to prevent further progression to complete retinal detachment. So kindly do see a retina specialist. Let me know how it went. Take care.
response: Hi, Thanks for writing in. The symptoms that you describe are suggestive of posterior vitreous detachment. This is caused by a separation of the vitreous gel from the back of the eye which causes it to pull on the retina causing flashing lights and floaters. It is usually harmless and does not require any treatment. However, if there is sudden increase in floaters, then you need to get your vision checked immediately as this can be a sign of hemorrhage or tear in the retina. Please do see an Ophthalmologist at once. Hope this helps.

doctor_response: Hi. I have gone through his reports (attachment removed to protect patient identity). Wall motion abnormality is seen in the echo report of your father. The heart is supplied by three arteries LAD, RCA, and LCX that is, left anterior descending artery, right coronary artery and left circumflex artery respectively. Any obstruction in blood supply in these vessels will cause decreased blood supply to a particular area of heart (which is supplied by that artery). As blood supply is compromised the muscles in that part of heart will not get proper nutrition and will start degenerating, which is medically termed as regional wall motion abnormality (RWMA). A coronary angiogram should be done to rule out coronary artery disease (blockage in the coronary artery), which is the main reason for RWMA and decreased ejection fraction. My advice is to get a coronary angiogram to rule out the blockage in the coronary artery.

In your fathers case his LVEF was reduced from 45% to 30-35%, this means that he has significant reduction in cardiac function. This could be due to many reasons like coronary artery disease or valvular heart disease. I would suggest my patients to have regular follow up with their consultant cardiologist and get investigated accordingly. Hope this helps.

question: Hello doctor,What is the stigma around mental health? Why it is there? How can people help break the stigma around mental health and what advice do you have for people who want help but stigma is keeping them from getting it?

Making people believe that mental illnesses are like any other medical illnesses, and these occur because of change in neuro-transmitters also help in reducing stigma.

People need to understand that mental health problems are just like any other physical disease and should be treated with respect and dignity. doctor_response: Hi. I have gone through your query. Prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP) has been replaced by PSA (prostate-specific antigen test). response: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP) are both enzymes that are found in the prostate gland. PSA is produced by the epithelial cells of the prostate gland and is released into the bloodstream. It can be detected in the blood as early as five years before any clinical signs of prostate cancer appear. PAP is produced by the smooth muscle cells of the prostate gland and is released into the semen. Elevated levels of PAP may indicate inflammation or obstruction of the prostate ducts. It is not a routine test but is sometimes used to monitor patients with prostate problems such as benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

question: Hello doctor,What is seasonal affective disorder and recommend products that can help people manage their symptoms?
doctor_response: Hello. Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a type of depression related to seasonal changes. I would like to call it winter mood changes as it often happens during the winter time. With regards to treatment, often advise increasing lightening of the place where the patient lives. Being in contact with people will help overcome the mood changes. response: Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) is a type of depression that occurs at certain times of the year, usually during the winter months when there is less natural sunlight. It is believed to be caused by changes in the amount of light to which an individual is exposed. The most common treatment for SAD is light therapy. Light therapy is the use of artificial light to replace lack of exposure to natural light, or to supplement it. This therapy involves sitting in front of a special light box that provides bright white light. For best results, one should sit in front of the light box for about 30 minutes each day from early morning until noon. Other forms of light therapy include dawn simulation, which simulates the natural rising of the sun, and blue light therapy, which uses a special lamp that produces only blue light.

question: Hi doctor, I was diagnosed with dengue towards the end of last month. I was hospitalized for five days. I went through a lot during that period and since coming out of the hospital, I have developed this phobia that I might have dengue again because my area is dengue prone with lots of mosquitoes. Whenever a mosquito bites me, I get filled with this fear that I might have dengue again.When I went to my doctor with this fear, he told me dengue does not happen twice in the same season, it can happen again in the next season, but it cannot happen again this season.I want to ask if this is true? If it is true, then what is the logic behind that? Can you please explain? I am immensely afraid of the disease.
doctor_response: Hello, Welcome to Chat Doctor forum. The fact that dengue cannot happen in the same season is true to some extent but not absolutely. Let me explain. Dengue is a viral infection caused by the bite of infected ades aegypti mosquito. Every mosquito bite will not lead to dengue fever as for infection to happen. First, the mosquito should be infected by the dengue virus (DEV). By infection of the mosquito I mean, the mosquito just serves as a vector or carrier for virus transfer to humans. Also, every mosquito carrying the dengue virus would not lead to dengue fever, shock, etc. Some people just have subclinical, asymptomatic infections too. There are actually four types of dengue viruses numbered from 1 to 4. Infection with one type, followed by recovery confers immunity to that type of infection. Our body produces antibodies against the virus and protects us from further infection, with time these antibodies fade away. So immunity in DEV is present but is short-lived. It can be said that the infection cannot occur in the same season, but if an infection with another type say (DEV type 1 followed by DEV type 2) occurs, the body does not have antibodies which are protective against type 2, as the body was previously infected by DEV type 1. This type of infection is more dangerous. However, in a season only one type of DEV infection occurs usually. I hope this helps.
response: 1-you should not be worried about getting dengue fever, as you have had dengue once before, it is highly unlikely that you will get it again.2-The logic is that your body has developed antibodies against the virus which protects you from getting dengue fever again.3-However, if you live in an area where dengue fever is endemic, there is always a chance that you may get dengue fever again due to the fact that the dengue virus is constantly mutating and changing its genetic makeup.4-Therefore, you must take precautions to avoid being bitten by mosquitoes and other insects by wearing long sleeves and using insect repellent.5-Also, do not forget to empty any stagnant water around your house or workplace where mosquitoes breed. Hope this helps
